title: bug: submit_plan keeps a re-planned task's stored effort with no tier minimum when effort is omitted, so a plan the size floor raises to heavy is stored and launched at effort high, below heavy's xhigh minimum, while the same plan with effort high passed explicitly is raised to xhigh
description:
Filed by defect hunt #15 (task-928a468d), lane 2 (the plan intake gates). Verified at HEAD d5431577 in a git-archive snapshot outside the shared checkout.

PROBLEM
- packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/submitPlan.ts:516-520: a requested effort is clamped and then raised to effortFloor(tier, …).
- submitPlan.ts:522-523: when the task already has an effort, the code is `effort = clampEffort(effort ? maxEffort(effort, task.effort) : task.effort, …)`. With effort omitted, that is task.effort clamped to the allowed list, with no effortFloor(tier).
- So take a row whose earlier standard-tier plan stored effort high, re-planned into the heavy band (6+ distinct files, or tier heavy passed). It is stored at tier heavy with effort high.
- resolveLaunch (src/util/routing.ts:261) passes a stored effort through clampEffort only. So the claim_next_task launch hint is heavy/high too.
- Every path back to PLANNING keeps tier and effort: a human plan reject, a critique block, request_replan, the qa_reject auto-replan. A re-plan with a stored effort is therefore the normal case.

CONTRACT
- docs/MCP_SERVER.md:388 (### moe.submit_plan, "Launch effort and models"): effort is raised "to the tier minimum (light/standard high, heavy xhigh), and never below the task's existing effort".
- The code's own comment at submitPlan.ts:506-510 says the effort is raised to "the tier minimum".
- The sibling branch for an explicit effort (submitPlan.ts:516-520) applies the floor.

EVIDENCE
- Repro: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-928a468d/B/replanEffortFloor.test.ts. Copy it into packages/moe-daemon/src/__hunt__/ of a d5431577 snapshot and run `npx vitest run src/__hunt__/replanEffortFloor.test.ts`.
- The test seeds a PLANNING row with {tier: standard, effort: high} and re-plans it with 6 distinct files, which puts planSizeFloor at heavy.
- Result: 3 failed, 1 passed. The passing control uses an explicit effort high, which is raised to xhigh.
  - × an omitted effort on the heavy re-plan never runs below the heavy minimum (xhigh). AssertionError: expected [ 'xhigh', 'max' ] to include 'high'
  - × the claim-time worker launch hint for that stored row is below xhigh too: the same assertion.
  - × an explicit tier heavy with effort omitted never runs below xhigh either: the same assertion.
- Output: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-928a468d/B/replanEffortFloor.output.txt
- Exposure: 0 of the 197 live heavy rows sit below xhigh, so this is a guard gap, not a live incident. Its precondition is common, though: 130 of 614 routed rows have planRevision ≥ 3.

FIX DIRECTION
- Apply effortFloor(tier, settings, lowEffortEligible) to the stored-effort branch's result too, so no branch can store an effort below the tier minimum. Report the raise through the existing effortRaised field.
- Also floor a stored effort in resolveLaunch by effortFloor(task.tier, settings, low). Then an older row, or one written over /ws, can never launch below its tier minimum.

FILES
- packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/submitPlan.ts
- packages/moe-daemon/src/util/routing.ts
- packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/submitPlan.effortFloor.test.ts (new)
- docs/MCP_SERVER.md: sync your own section, `### moe.submit_plan`. Its Launch effort note (:388) already states the floor. Say there that the floor also applies to a kept stored effort and to the claim-time launch hint.

Placement: no open row holds these files at filing time. Two held-back plan-intake leads also edit submitPlan.ts, so they wait for this row:
- the plan sanitizer keeps 50 steps while submit_plan and taskSizing.maxSteps allow 100;
- planningNotes has no type or length check.

resolveLaunch on a WORKING row stored as {tier: heavy, effort: high} returns an effort of at least xhigh, while a light or standard row stored at high still launches at high (new test)

It ports the hunt repro /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-928a468d/B/replanEffortFloor.test.ts and adds controls.

The setup seeds a PLANNING row at {tier: 'standard', effort: 'high'}. The cases:
(1) Control: an explicit effort 'high' on a 6-file re-plan is raised to 'xhigh'. It passes before and after the fix.
(2) An omitted effort on that re-plan, which planSizeFloor makes heavy: the stored effort is 'xhigh' or 'max', and the response launch.effort and resolveLaunch(stored row) both equal it.
(3) An explicit tier 'heavy' with effort omitted is floored the same way.
(4) Control: a 1-step, 3-file re-plan stays standard and keeps effort 'high' (the light/standard floor is high).
(5) resolveLaunch on WORKING rows:
  - heavy/high → xhigh;
  - heavy/max → max;
  - standard/high → high;
  - light/high → high;
  - a lowEffortEligible heavy/low row keeps low, because a docs/tests-only row has no tier minimum.

Architect RED proof at 0f56d3a7: 3 failed (cases 2, 3, 5), 2 passed (1, 4).

implementationPlan.description:
The fix: two expressions, both wrapped in the existing helpers maxEffort and effortFloor. Line numbers are from 0f56d3a7.

(1) packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/submitPlan.ts:522-524. In the `if (task.effort)` branch, the stored-effort path, change `effort = clampEffort(effort ? maxEffort(effort, task.effort) : task.effort, project.settings, lowEffortEligible);` to `effort = maxEffort(clampEffort(…same args…), effortFloor(tier, project.settings, lowEffortEligible));`. Add a 2-3 line comment saying why: a kept stored effort still meets the tier minimum when a re-plan lands in a higher tier.
  - effortFloor is already imported (:16).
  - It returns undefined for a docs/tests-only plan, and maxEffort(a, undefined) is a, so low efforts are unchanged.
  - The explicit-effort branch at :516-520 is untouched.

(2) packages/moe-daemon/src/util/routing.ts:261, resolveLaunch's stored-effort branch. `isEffort(task.effort) ? clampEffort(task.effort, settings, low) : tierEffort(task.tier, settings)` becomes `isEffort(task.effort) ? maxEffort(clampEffort(task.effort, settings, low), effortFloor(task.tier, settings, low)) : tierEffort(task.tier, settings)`, with a one-line comment: an older row, or one written outside submit_plan, never launches below its tier minimum.
  - The qa role's later maxEffort with the qa floor is unchanged.

Error handling needs no new branch. An unknown stored effort is already caught by isEffort in resolveLaunch, and in submit_plan clampEffort maps a garbage value up to the lowest allowed level before the floor applies.

Do not change effortRaised: it reports only a raise of a requested effort.

Reference: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-87cba58c/prototype.diff (32 lines). Edit with your own editor (Edit on Claude, apply_patch on codex exec).

executionContract.intendedBehavior: No task is stored or launched below its tier's effort minimum (light/standard high, heavy xhigh) unless it is docs/tests-only. A re-plan that omits effort keeps the task's stored effort, raised to the minimum of the tier the re-plan lands in, exactly as an explicit effort already is. resolveLaunch, which builds claim_next_task's and submit_plan's launch hint, applies the same minimum to a stored effort. An older row, or one written outside submit_plan, therefore never launches below its tier minimum.
acceptanceCriteria: A PLANNING row stored at {tier: standard, effort: high}, re-planned with 6 distinct files and no effort, is stored as heavy with effort xhigh or max, and submit_plan's launch hint carries the same effort.
An explicit tier heavy with effort omitted is floored the same way.
resolveLaunch returns xhigh for a WORKING heavy/high row and high for light/high and standard/high rows. A lowEffortEligible row keeps its low effort.
docs/MCP_SERVER.md's ### moe.submit_plan says the minimum also applies to a kept stored effort and to the launch hint.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Two alternatives were rejected:
(1) Start an omitted effort from tierEffort, the tier default, and take the max with the stored effort. That would also bump a standard row stored at high to xhigh on every re-plan, which changes accepted behaviour beyond the bug. Flooring alone fixes the contract violation.
(2) Floor only in submit_plan. resolveLaunch would still launch older below-floor rows at their stored effort, which is why the row names both sites.

- resolveLaunch feeds both submit_plan's response launch hint and claim_next_task's.
